owned_invariants: The roots of a task are a nonempty list of exact rationals. The expected polynomial is the expanded product of (x - r) over the roots, coefficients highest degree first.

A reply is text holding a JSON object with a nonempty list under coefficients. A coefficient is canonical as a JSON integer, or as text p/q in lowest terms with q above 1 and no sign but a leading minus.

classify gives the first that applies: MALFORMED_JSON when the text is not that object or a coefficient is no number in any notation; RATIONAL_NONCANONICAL when every coefficient is a number but one is written another way; NONMONIC_LEADING_COEFFICIENT when the first coefficient is not 1; CLEAN when the coefficients are the expected ones; SIGN_MISMATCH when the sizes are right and a sign is wrong; WRONG_VALUE otherwise.
Noncanonical writing is reported before any value is compared, so a right answer written loosely is not clean.
EPITOPES lists the five kinds of mistake in the order they are looked for.
boundaries: classify sorts a reply; it does not say how to fix it. What a caller tells the model about a kind of mistake is the caller's text.
The loose-number pattern decides only between malformed and noncanonical. No value is ever taken from a loosely written number.
The degree is bounded by the caller: expanding n roots costs n squared rational products.
